title: Altered intestinal absorption of L-thyroxine caused by coffee
authors: Benvenga S, Bartolone L, Pappalardo MA, Russo A, Lapa D, Giorgianni G, et al.
population: Eight women with inappropriately high TSH when T4 was swallowed with coffee or espresso, six of whom underwent absorption tests, and nine volunteers; plus in vitro recovery tests
funder: Funding statement not read: the publisher's full text returned HTTP 403 to automated access.
result: Two 100 µg T4 tablets were swallowed with coffee, water, or water followed 60 minutes later by coffee, and serum T4 followed for 4 hours. Against water, coffee lowered the average incremental rise of serum T4 by 36% in patients and 29% in volunteers, the peak rise by 30% and 19%, and the area under the curve by 36% and 27%, and delayed the maximal rise by 38 and 43 minutes; coffee taken 60 minutes after water had no effect. Bran interfered more than coffee. Results read from the PubMed abstract.
